bill.title: Ending Improper Payments to Deceased People Act

industries.rationale: Life insurers and annuity providers rely on death records to process claims and prevent fraudulent payments to deceased beneficiaries.
Banks and financial institutions use death records to manage accounts, prevent fraud, and comply with payment verification requirements.

bill.plainSummary: This bill makes permanent the Treasury Department's access to Social Security death records to prevent payments from being sent to deceased individuals. It requires the Social Security Administration to have clear and convincing evidence before marking someone as deceased in its master file. If someone is incorrectly listed as dead, the SSA can notify federal and state agencies that provide benefits so the error can be corrected.

bill.title: Patients Deserve Price Tags Act
bill.latestActionText: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 522.
subjects: Department of Health and Human Services
Drug safety, medical device, and laboratory regulation

industries.rationale: The bill directly imposes new price-disclosure obligations on hospitals and surgical centers, changing their administrative and compliance requirements.
Medical device costs must be included in the price estimates, affecting how device manufacturers' products are priced and disclosed to patients.
Price transparency requirements may affect how insurers negotiate rates and how patients understand their coverage and out-of-pocket costs.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would require hospitals, ambulatory surgical centers, and other healthcare facilities to provide patients with upfront price estimates for scheduled procedures and services. The estimates would need to include costs for the facility, physicians, anesthesia, medical devices, and other associated charges. Facilities that fail to provide these price disclosures could face civil penalties.

bill.title: Expedited Access to Biosimilars Act
bill.latestActionText: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 520.
subjects: Drug safety, medical device, and laboratory regulation

industries.rationale: The bill directly addresses the regulatory approval process for biosimilar drugs, which would affect pharmaceutical and biotech manufacturers' market access and competitive landscape.
Faster biosimilar approval could reduce drug costs that health insurers cover, affecting their reimbursement obligations and formulary decisions.
Changes to biosimilar availability may affect which medications hospitals and physician groups can prescribe and the costs they incur for specialty drugs.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would create a faster approval pathway for biosimilar drugs—lower-cost alternatives to expensive biologic medications. The source material provides only the title and subject terms, which indicate the bill addresses drug regulation and licensing but does not specify what procedural or regulatory changes would be made. Without bill text or a summary, the exact mechanisms for expediting biosimilar access cannot be described.

bill.title: National Plan for Epilepsy Act
bill.latestActionText: Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.

industries.rationale: The bill's focus on epilepsy treatment, diagnosis, and cure research directly affects pharmaceutical and medical device companies developing epilepsy therapies.
The national plan's coordination of epilepsy care and services would affect hospitals and health systems that diagnose and treat epilepsy patients.

bill.plainSummary: This bill directs the Department of Health and Human Services to create and carry out a national plan to address epilepsy, including prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and research coordination across federal agencies. HHS must establish an advisory council that reports to Congress every two years and must itself submit annual progress reports with recommended actions. These requirements would remain in effect until the end of 2035.

bill.title: Accelerating Access to Critical Therapies for ALS Reauthorization Act of 2026
bill.latestActionText: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 461.
subjects: Department of Health and Human Services

industries.rationale: The bill directly funds research and development of drugs and therapies for ALS and neurodegenerative diseases, affecting pharmaceutical and biotech companies developing these treatments.
Clinical trial enrollment requirements and expanded access to investigational drugs may affect hospitals and health systems conducting ALS research and treatment.

bill.plainSummary: This bill extends funding through fiscal year 2031 for federal programs that support research and development of treatments for ALS (Lou Gehrig's disease) and similar neurodegenerative diseases. It requires the National Institutes of Health to track safety data more closely when awarding grants for experimental drug studies, and directs the Food and Drug Administration to publish five-year plans describing how it will help develop and approve treatments for these rare diseases. The bill also mandates reports evaluating the effectiveness of these grant programs.

bill.title: HALT Fentanyl Act

industries.rationale: The bill changes registration and licensing requirements for pharmaceutical researchers conducting controlled substance research and affects the regulatory classification of chemical substances.
The bill establishes new criminal penalties and quantity thresholds that will affect prosecution and defense of drug trafficking cases.
Universities and research institutions conducting controlled substance research would be subject to the new registration processes and requirements established by the bill.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would permanently classify all fentanyl-related substances as Schedule I controlled substances, meaning they would be treated as having high abuse potential and no accepted medical use. It sets the same criminal penalties and quantity thresholds for fentanyl-related substances as currently apply to fentanyl analogues. The bill also creates a streamlined registration process for researchers studying Schedule I substances and relaxes some requirements for research facilities working with controlled substances.

plain.whoItTouches: People caught up in the criminal law, and victims of crime.

bill.title: A joint resolution proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States relating to contributions and expenditures intended to affect elections.
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

industries.rationale: Organizations that spend money to influence elections would face new potential restrictions on their expenditures and fundraising.
The amendment would create new constitutional authority to regulate campaign finance, directly affecting election law practice and lobbying activity.
Limits on campaign spending could affect demand for political advertising across broadcast, digital, and print media platforms.
The amendment's authorization to distinguish between natural persons and corporations could affect how financial institutions participate in election-related spending.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution proposes a constitutional amendment that would allow Congress and state governments to set limits on how much money candidates and others can raise and spend to influence elections. It would also permit lawmakers to treat corporations and other legal entities differently from individual people, including by prohibiting those entities from spending money on elections. The amendment would require ratification by three-fourths of the states to take effect.

bill.title: Secure Rural Schools Reauthorization Act of 2025

industries.rationale: The program directly funds schools in rural counties containing federal land.
The program funds road construction and maintenance projects in affected counties.
Counties with federal land often have timber and mineral extraction activities that may be affected by resource advisory committee project decisions.

bill.plainSummary: This bill extends a federal program that sends payments to rural counties containing national forests and other federal land. The money helps fund local schools, roads, and municipal services. The bill provides payments through fiscal year 2026, including back payments for 2024 and 2025, and allows counties and advisory committees to continue initiating projects through 2028.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
